column1: # Partition table: how the board's 4 MB of flash memory is divided.
# Each line is one partition: Name
# Offsets and sizes are in hexadecimal bytes. The first 0x9000 bytes of flash
# are not listed: they hold the bootloader and this table itself.
# Changing this file moves the partitions
column2: so afterwards both the firmware and

column1: # the filesystem image have to be uploaded again.
# The layout uses the whole chip
# nvs       20 KB. Small key-value storage used by the system
#           radio calibration and the last WiFi connection. It ends at 0xE000
#           on purpose: with every firmware upload
#           writes 8 KB of boot data at 0xE000
#           between there and the firmware at 0x10000.
# factory   1920 KB. The firmware. A single copy
#           updating over WiFi would need two. The release build fills about
#           68% of it and the debug build about 72%
column2: so there is space to grow.

column1: # spiffs    2048 KB. The filesystem holding the database (about 816 KB).
#           The subtype is called spiffs for historical reasons;
#           it is formatted and used as LittleFS (see board_build.filesystem in
#           platformio.ini). It occupies exactly the second half of the chip
#           less the last 64 KB.
# coredump  64 KB. When the firmware crashes
column2: the framework saves the state of

column1: #           every task here before restarting
column2: so the crash can be examined

column1: #           afterwards. The framework is built to do this and only needs the

nvs
